Hi Neha —

Thanks for taking the time on the call today. As promised I attached our high-level usage sketch (pegasus_usage_samples.json) and a short PDF with the feature set we expect to run in production (pegasus_memory_request.pdf). To confirm the key inputs that matter for sizing: 

- Primary model: open variant similar to Llama-2 70B (we'll share the exact checkpoint once legal finishes).
- Typical prompt + response working set: 10–20k tokens for most sequences; 1–2% of traffic will reach ~64k tokens during long-form summarization.
- Peak concurrent sessions: 45 sustained, 120 burst for short windows (10–15 minutes).
- Target P95 latency for interactive UIs: <= 450ms; background batch jobs can be 2–4s.
- Expected monthly token volume: ~4B tokens.

We'd like Redwood to propose a committed/dedicated pool with a staging trial. Procurement is willing to move fast if we can show predictable cost and a fallback plan (e.g., smaller quantized variant).

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up with Marcus or the infra lead if useful.

Subject: Re: Initial capacity discussion — preliminary assumptions

Summarizing internal assumptions for the Pegasus footprint sketch (will refine after Neha confirms exact token distribution):

Assumptions:
- Model baseline: ~70B dense transformer; baseline weights ~140 GB (FP16) but we serve quantized variants to fit on typical 80GB GPUs.
- KV-cache: 32 bytes per token (key+value + headers) per layer — for a 70B dense architecture with 64 layers that maps to roughly 2.0 KB per token; this is an upper-bound conservative number we use for planning.
- Typical session working set (no offload):
  - FP16 baseline (no quant): model weights + activations + KV cache -> ~120 GB per concurrent sequence (not feasible on a single 80 GB card for very long contexts).
  - 4-bit quantized model (INT4-style / q4_k_m): weight storage reduced ~4x -> model weights ~35 GB on-device. With KV cache for 20k tokens -> ~40 GB extra; headroom points to 1 session per 80GB GPU at 20k tokens, ~0.3 sessions at 64k.

Sizing notes / recommended architecture choices:
- Hybrid approach: reserve a baseline pool of 6 x H100-80GB equivalents for interactive traffic (assumes sharded model placement + KV caching) to meet sustained 45 concurrent sessions at typical 10–20k lengths using quantized variants.
- Burst and long-context path: implement a fallback tier (lower-cost spot or higher-latency nodes) for the rare 64k sessions and background summarization jobs. This could be handled by temporary model variant fallback + progressive KV offload to NVMe.
- Latency target vs batching: to hit 450ms P95 we recommend small micro-batches (batch size 1–4) on H100-class GPUs with pinned KV in GPU memory; A100 80GB is possible but expect ~10–20% higher latency for same load.

Preliminary numbers (very rough):
- Baseline committed pool: 6 x H100-80GB (covering interactive quantized variant at 45 sustained concurrent sessions, with ~15% headroom).
- Additional burst capacity: 4 x A100-80GB (as preemptible/elastic) to absorb 120 concurrent short bursts and 64k long-context offloads.
- Trial footprint: two-week reserved pool of 4 H100 + 2 A100 to validate telemetry and refine model variant thresholds.

I'll convert this into a one-page table and accompanying cost delta estimate (FP16 vs 4-bit) for procurement. Priyom, can you add any constraints around KV offload runtime and expected NVMe throughput needed?

— Marcus
Senior Systems Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity discussion — offload/ops considerations

Notes on KV offload and ops implications (for Neha to share with Pegasus):

- NVMe offload profile: expect ~0.8–1.2 MB/sec per token for read-heavy long-context retrieval when using our progressive chunked offload (depends on PCIe gen and flash tier). For a 64k sequence this implies sustained NVMe bandwidth of ~50–75 MB/s per session during reconstruction; parallelism needed for multiple concurrent long contexts.
- Warm-up and cold-cache effects: first pass long-context sessions incur extra CPU and NVMe IO; plan for a 10–30% effective latency multiplier for sessions that trigger on-disk rehydration.
- Quantization accuracy risk: q4 variants generally preserve generation quality for most tasks; medical-quality summarization might need q5/FP16 for final outputs — propose decode-time fallback where we do final re-score / re-generation on FP16 smaller shard if quality thresholds fail.
- Ops surface: rolling reserve pool sizing (6 H100 baseline + 4 A100 burst) requires automated scaling gates, cost-aware routing, and a small ops playbook: 
  1) Canary deploy quantized variant to 10% traffic for 48 hours.
  2) Collect perplexity/ROUGE QA checks on the canary traffic; if QA passes, increase to 50% then 100%.
  3) Enable NVMe offload quotas and set alerts for NVMe saturation > 70%.

Will prepare the NVMe bandwidth table and quick runbook — can attach as a sheet in the proposal.

— Priyom
Inference Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood proposal: committed pool + trial for Pegasus (summary)

Alice — we pulled together a pragmatic committed plan and a two-week proof-of-concept reservation to validate latency and quality tradeoffs. Attaching a short PDF (redwood_proposal_v1.pdf) and an Excel sheet with the preliminary per-GPU memory math (pegasus_memory_estimate.xlsx). Summary below: 

What we recommend (TL;DR):
- Two-week trial: 4 x H100-80GB + 2 x A100-80GB reserved for a focused validation (we monitor P95 latency, NVMe usage, and QA metrics).
- Committed recommended pool: 6 x H100-80GB dedicated for interactive traffic using quantized model variants (expected to cover 45 sustained sessions at 10–20k tokens with ~15% headroom).
- Elastic burst: 4 x A100-80GB for preemptible/elastic capacity to handle 120-concurrency bursts and offload-heavy 64k runs.
- Model variant approach: start with q4_k_m quantized variant for the majority of traffic; decode-time re-score/fallback to FP16 for clinical/high-accuracy outputs.
- Ops playbook: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48–96 hours, NVMe saturation alerts, and an SLO-based rollback policy.

Next steps we suggest: 
1) Procurement: a short SOW and a two-week PO to spin up trial reserved pool.
2) Technical: share a sample of exact checkpoints and a small prompt set for our QA harness.
3) Commercial: we'll provide a two-line committed pricing addendum for the H100 reserved hours vs burst on A100.

If this looks good I can send a formal SOW + cost sheet by EOD tomorrow.

Best —
Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
